major_arcana.story: The musical journey of The Sound of Music - from Maria's solitary communion with nature, through her arrival at the von Trapp household, the awakening of love and music in a family haunted by loss, the looming shadow of the Anschluss, and the ultimate escape over the mountains. Each song marks a transformation: the abbey trying to contain wildness, children learning to sing, a captain remembering his heart, lovers recognizing each other, and a family choosing freedom over compliance. The story asks: how do we preserve authentic joy and love when instrumental forces demand our submission?
major_arcana.visual_style: Cinematic wide-screen compositions in lush Technicolor - the rich production values of the 1965 film. Sweeping alpine vistas, ornate interiors of abbey and villa, theatrical staging. Strong use of light (sunlight on mountains, candlelight in abbey, spotlight on stage). Romantic realism with moments of expressionist drama. The aesthetic should feel like film stills - composed, dramatic, emotionally resonant. Colors shift from natural greens and blues (early cards) through warm golds and reds (middle) to dramatic shadows and escaping dawn light (late cards).

ranks.name: The Sound of Music
ranks.description: Maria alone on the mountain, arms wide, spinning in pure connection with nature before duty calls her back. The primordial moment of authentic creative expression.

inverted: Inability to integrate joy with duty

ranks.visual_content: A lone figure on a mountain meadow, arms outstretched, surrounded by wildflowers and distant peaks, bathed in golden light

ranks.name: Alleluia
ranks.description: The abbey at prayer, sacred space, the structure that transmits devotion across generations. Authentic transmission through ritual.
ranks.visual_content: Stone abbey interior with vaulted ceilings, nuns in prayer, candlelight and incense, stained glass casting colored light

ranks.name: Maria
ranks.description: The nuns singing about the problem of Maria - a flibbertigibbet, a will-o'-the-wisp, a clown. The question of how wildness fits within structure.

upright: The problem you pose to systems

ranks.visual_content: Multiple perspectives converging - whispered conversations, hands gesturing, a central figure conspicuously absent or glimpsed through windows

ranks.name: I Have Confidence
ranks.description: Walking toward the von Trapp villa, nervous but determined. Stepping into the unknown with self-encouragement bordering on self-deception.

inverted: Walking into disaster with a smile

ranks.visual_content: A figure on a tree-lined path approaching a grand house, luggage in hand, posture caught between hesitation and determination

ranks.name: Sixteen Going On Seventeen
ranks.description: Liesl and Rolf in the gazebo, dancing in the rain. Young love, innocence, romantic ideals before reality intrudes.
ranks.visual_content: Two young figures dancing in a glass gazebo during a rainstorm, graceful and fragile, lightning in the distance

ranks.name: My Favorite Things
ranks.description: Maria comforting the frightened children during a thunderstorm. Teaching resilience through redirecting attention to joy.
ranks.visual_content: A nurturing figure surrounded by children in a bedroom, storm outside windows, small beautiful objects and memories made visible

ranks.name: Do-Re-Mi
ranks.description: Teaching the children to sing throughout Salzburg - the fountain, the steps, the bicycles. Music as pedagogy, connection forming through learning.
ranks.visual_content: A progression through city landmarks - fountain, market, bicycle procession - figures in matching outfits learning and playing

ranks.name: The Lonely Goatherd
ranks.description: The puppet show - Maria and children performing together. Instrumental creation in its most charming form, teaching through constructed spectacle.
ranks.visual_content: A miniature theater stage with marionettes, visible strings, hands controlling from above, children and adult performing together

ranks.name: Edelweiss
ranks.description: The Captain singing for the first time since his wife's death. The flower of Austria, memory, homeland, grief beginning to transform.
ranks.visual_content: A man with a guitar, eyes distant, remembering. A small white alpine flower in focus, mountains beyond

ranks.name: Grand Waltz
ranks.description: The formal party at the villa - wealth, social performance, the world of the Baroness and Max. Structure and display.
ranks.visual_content: Ballroom in golden light, couples in formal wear waltzing in perfect formation, chandeliers, wealth and ritual

ranks.name: Laendler
ranks.description: Maria and the Captain dancing the Austrian folk dance, the moment of recognition, the exact instant everything changes.
ranks.visual_content: Two figures in a folk dance, hands almost touching, eyes meeting, the world stopping around them, twilight in the courtyard

ranks.name: So Long, Farewell
ranks.description: The children performing at the party. Innocence on display, but also the song they'll later use as cover for escape. Performance as both gift and strategy.
ranks.visual_content: Children on a grand staircase in nightclothes, guests watching below, each child in spotlight briefly before ascending into shadow

ranks.name: Processional Waltz
ranks.description: Formal instrumental music, ceremony, the structures of traditional society. The forms that can either support or constrain.
ranks.visual_content: Formal procession, architectural grandeur, symmetry and order, figures moving in prescribed patterns, gold and marble

ranks.name: Goodbye Maria / How Can Love Survive Waltz
ranks.description: Maria fleeing back to the abbey, the Baroness's cynical question. Crisis - can authentic love survive in the world of wealth and power?

inverted: Belief that nothing good can last

ranks.visual_content: Split composition - a figure running away in darkness, and an elegant woman in jewels asking an unanswerable question

ranks.name: Edelweiss Waltz
ranks.description: Variation on the earlier theme, musical echo, the same song in a different context. Repetition with transformation.
ranks.visual_content: Musical notation showing variations on a theme, or the same scene viewed from a different angle, shadows shifted

ranks.name: Entr'acte
ranks.description: Intermission, the pause between acts. Time passing, the breath before the storm, transition, the in-between.
ranks.visual_content: Empty stage, curtains, house lights, or a still moment - dawn or dusk, in-between light, anticipation

ranks.name: Climb Ev'ry Mountain
ranks.description: Mother Superior telling Maria to go back, to follow her authentic calling. The most direct statement of the film's thesis: seek your dream.

upright: Every path until you find your dream

ranks.visual_content: A wise elder figure giving counsel, mountains rising behind, a path winding upward into mist, benediction and sending-forth

ranks.name: Something Good
ranks.description: Maria and the Captain in the gazebo (same place as Liesl's innocent romance), recognizing mature love. 'Somewhere in my youth or childhood, I must have done something good.'

inverted: Waiting for the other shoe to drop

ranks.visual_content: Two adults in the moonlit gazebo, equal and tender, architectural symmetry suggesting both the earlier scene and its transformation

ranks.name: Processional and Maria (The Wedding)
ranks.description: The wedding ceremony, union, but also the moment the Nazis are searching for them. Completion and danger converging, joy against threat.
ranks.visual_content: Wedding ceremony in the abbey, bride and groom, but shadows lengthening, sense of urgency, beauty and threat intertwined
